newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal Telecom boosts new businesses.
newsitem.headline: Portugal Telecom boosts new businesses.

text.p: Portugal Telecom said on Wednesday that emerging businesses -- mobile phones, cable TV and data transmission -- increased their share of overall group turnover in 1996 to 11.4 percent in 1996 from 8.3 percent the year before.
Consolidated operating revenues were 477.8 billion escudos, up 11.3 percent on the previous year.
In a statement accompanying its 1996 results, the company said that fixed telephone services continued to show steady growth, with turnover rising 5.8 percent to 345.9 billion escudos last year.
Domestic phone service income rose 11 percent to 263.7 billion escudos but international services were down 8.1 percent at 82.2 billion.

It said that its strategic priorities remain to increase telephone penetration, which rose to 38.5 percent in December 1996 from 36.7 percent a year earlier, rebalance tariffs by reducing long distance and international charges and improve the quality of service, especially to major accounts.

It noted that pension costs were stable at around 33.7 billion but this masked a sharp increase in curtailment losses related to early retirements which rose from 12.4 billion to 18.1 billion in 1996.
The company said that it remained on track to meet its target of a 97 percent rate in digitilisation in local switching by 1998 against 79.4 percent at the end of 1997.
The average increase in prices for fixed telephone services was 1.9 percent in nominal terms last year.
Telepac, the company's data communications arm, boosted operating revenues by 11.3 percent to 13.8 billion escudos.
Cable television services recorded a 223 percent rise in operating revenues to 4.9 billion escudos.
